conclusion_detail.narrative:
The run found a mixed answer. NVDA’s margin advantage over AAPL and MSFT was supported as a durable profitability difference, but the idea that faster revenue growth over the same periods explains that advantage remained unresolved.

The first claim held with strong support and no refuting evidence: NVDA’s net margin advantage looked like a real profitability difference, not something fully explained away by growth. The second claim also had substantial supporting evidence, but it did not reach a settled conclusion, so the growth explanation was not confirmed or rejected.

The evidence came from a correlation analysis, then a simple regression, then another correlation analysis. The loop stopped because it had sufficient evidence for a mixed verdict, but two questions remained open: whether the margin advantage persisted across periods or was only a one-off spike, and whether controlling for revenue growth would remove most or all of the margin gap.
